title: Multi-modal, Sun angle and scale invariant image correspondence using Chandrayaan-2 optical images (OHRC, TMC and IIRS)
department: Department of Space / Indian Space Research Organisation
dataset_link:
Specific datasets link will be provided - TBD

• Chandrayaan-2 orbiter optical payload: OHRC, TMC-2, IIRS lunar images. (Link: https://chmapbrowse.issdc.gov.in/)
• Reference: LRO NAC Images (Lunar Reconnaissance Orbiter Narrow Angle Camera) (Link: https://lroc.im.-ldi.com/images/downloads/ , https://quickmap.lroc.im-ldi.com/ ), SE
description:
Background Image Registration is the process of aligning two or more images of the same scene taken at different times, from different viewpoints, or by different sensors into a common coordinate system.
It has two main components:
• Source Image (Moving): The image that is to be geometrically transformed to align with the reference image.
• Reference Image (Fixed): The target image about which source image is to be geometrically transformed.
Description The process of lunar images registration involves finding match points between source and reference image and then aligning the source image with the reference image. The key challenges involved in this process are as follows:
• Illumination variation: Illumination variation refers to changes in sun azimuth and elevation effect on the surface lighting conditions that affect the appearance of the lunar surface features which is hard to correlate.
• Viewpoint variation: It refers to geometric distortions caused by different camera positions/orientations capturing the same scene. Objects appear shifted, scaled, rotated, or perspective-distorted depending on observing angle.
• Scale Variation: Lunar imaging missions operate at vastly different altitudes and at different spatial resolutions. This creates scale ratios.
Expected Solution Generic software solution for finding correspondence between Chandrayaan-2 acquired optical images and Lunar reference images with a sub-pixel accuracy of source image maintaining uniform distribution across the images.
• Software and registered product with corresponding match points.
• Evaluation metric (eg. RMSE, inlier match count, inlier ratio, etc.)
summary: Innovation (2/5): draws on standard software/hardware techniques applied to a space technology problem, placing it in the incremental band. Feasibility (3/5): as a software build with moderate integration complexity, a full build is tight for 36 hours and will need scope-cutting. Impact (2/5): addresses a more targeted user group within Space Technology. Tech Depth (2/5): centers on multi-modal. Sustainability (3/5): will need a maintenance/upkeep plan post-hackathon. Scalability (2/5): currently scoped narrowly and would need rework to scale. Total 14/30 -> Red verdict.

detail.title: Multi-modal, Sun Angle and Scale Invariant Image Correspondence Using Chandrayaan-2 Optical Images (OHRC, TMC and IIRS)

overview.in_plain_terms: Build an algorithm that can automatically align lunar images taken by different Chandrayaan-2 cameras, at different times, with different sun angles and vastly different resolutions, into one common coordinate system, work that's currently very difficult because lighting changes make the same crater or rock look completely different.
overview.why_it_matters: Combining data from Chandrayaan-2's different instruments (OHRC, TMC, IIRS) requires accurate image alignment, but changing sun angles make this genuinely hard. Solving it directly unlocks more value from India's own lunar mission data.
pain_points: Sun angle/illumination variation makes the same lunar surface features look very different across images.
Different cameras (OHRC, TMC, IIRS) operate at vastly different resolutions and viewpoints.
Standard feature-matching techniques struggle with this combination of illumination and scale variation.
overview.background: Chandrayaan-2's OHRC, TMC, and IIRS instruments capture lunar imagery at different resolutions, times, and viewing conditions, and registering these images together for combined analysis is genuinely difficult due to illumination and scale variation.
overview.whats_being_asked: An image registration/correspondence algorithm robust to illumination (sun angle), viewpoint, and scale variation across multi-modal Chandrayaan-2 optical imagery (OHRC, TMC, IIRS).
expected_solution: Feature detection/matching robust to illumination variation.
Cross-scale correspondence across vastly different resolution imagery.
Validated alignment accuracy across real Chandrayaan-2 datasets.

analysis.innovation_scope_note: Moderate as scored. Illumination-invariant and multi-modal image registration is an active remote-sensing/computer-vision research area, genuine technical depth, though the score reflects real difficulty given the extreme conditions (lunar illumination, multi-sensor scale gaps).
analysis.invention_effort_note: Low as scored, but this significantly understates real difficulty, genuinely robust multi-modal, illumination-invariant, cross-scale registration is a hard, actively-researched computer vision problem, not a routine engineering task.

competitive_landscape.note: Requires genuine remote-sensing computer vision expertise and access to real Chandrayaan-2 imagery, an extremely specialized field.

innovation.note: Illumination-invariant, multi-modal registration is established research territory, genuine but not conceptually unprecedented.

invention.tag: High in reality, understated by the score
invention.note: Genuinely robust registration across these combined challenges (illumination, scale, multi-modal) is hard, active-research-level difficulty.

technical_feasibility.note: Real Chandrayaan-2 imagery access, extreme lunar illumination conditions, and multi-sensor scale gaps together make full robustness genuinely hard to achieve in 36 hours.

impact_and_benefits.note: Genuine value for lunar science and ISRO's own mission data utilization, a narrow, specialized scientific audience.

architecture.note: A feature-matching/registration pipeline, well-understood pattern applied to a genuinely hard combined-challenge problem.

overall_verdict.reasoning: Red, mainly reflecting genuine, real difficulty that the score doesn't fully capture. Scope your demo to one specific challenge dimension (e.g. illumination-invariance between two images with different sun angles at similar scale) rather than attempting full robustness across illumination, scale, and modality simultaneously.

evaluator_lens.biggest_strength: If real Chandrayaan-2 imagery is accessible (ISRO's public data archives), this gives genuine, real test data for a scientifically meaningful problem.
evaluator_lens.biggest_risk: Attempting full robustness across all three challenge dimensions (illumination, scale, multi-modal) simultaneously in 36 hours is very ambitious, most existing published research addresses these challenges incrementally, not all at once.
evaluator_lens.validate_before_commit: Scope to demonstrating robustness against one primary challenge dimension (illumination variation is the most explicitly emphasized in the problem background) using real accessible Chandrayaan-2 imagery, rather than claiming full multi-modal, cross-scale, illumination-invariant registration.

idea_0_4: Source real, publicly accessible Chandrayaan-2 imagery (OHRC/TMC/IIRS data from ISRO's public archives) for your test cases.
Choose your primary challenge focus: illumination-invariance is the most explicitly emphasized and most tractable starting point.
Split: one person on feature detection/matching, one on registration/alignment validation.
prototype_4_22: Build illumination-robust feature detection (techniques like SIFT variants or learned features designed for illumination invariance).
Build your matching and registration/alignment pipeline.
Test against real Chandrayaan-2 image pairs with different sun angles.
integration_22_30: Validate alignment accuracy against known reference points or overlapping features in your real test imagery.
Test on a genuinely challenging case (significant sun angle difference) to assess real robustness.
If time allows, extend to a secondary challenge (basic scale variation between two same-modality images).
polish_30_36: Build a clear visualization showing your registration result on real Chandrayaan-2 imagery, before and after alignment.
Rehearse presenting your alignment accuracy validation honestly, including any cases where registration struggled.
Prepare to discuss the gap between your scoped demonstration and full multi-modal, cross-scale robustness.
build_plan.how_to_stand_out: Show a real, challenging Chandrayaan-2 image pair with a significant sun-angle difference, and your algorithm successfully registering them with validated alignment accuracy, that real data plus honest, measured accuracy is far more credible than an unvalidated claim of full robustness across all challenge dimensions.

strengths: Real Chandrayaan-2 imagery is accessible from ISRO's public data archives, giving genuine test data.
Scoping to one primary challenge dimension is achievable and still scientifically meaningful.
weaknesses: Full robustness across illumination, scale, and modality simultaneously is genuinely hard, active-research-level difficulty.
Requires real remote-sensing computer vision expertise, a narrow, specialized skillset.

team_fit.ideal_ratio: CV-heavy, with real remote-sensing domain understanding.
team_fit.approach: Source real Chandrayaan-2 imagery early and scope to illumination-invariance as your primary, most tractable challenge dimension.

ai_buildability_split.ai_can_build_fast: Standard feature-detection and matching algorithm scaffolding.
ai_buildability_split.needs_human_judgment: Designing genuinely illumination-invariant features and validating registration accuracy against real lunar imagery's unique challenges, that requires real remote-sensing domain expertise.
ai_buildability_split.risk_of_leaning_on_ai_only: A registration algorithm validated only on easy, similar-illumination image pairs would not demonstrate the genuine robustness this PS is specifically testing for, which is explicitly the hard, illumination-variant case.

data_resource_availability.status: Real Chandrayaan-2 imagery (OHRC, TMC, IIRS) is accessible through ISRO's public planetary data archives.
data_resource_availability.backup_plan: Not needed, real data access is achievable here, though data volume and processing time should be planned for.

judge_qna.question: How robust is your registration to genuinely significant sun-angle differences, not just minor variation?
judge_qna.strong_answer: Present your validation results against real Chandrayaan-2 image pairs with the most significant illumination differences you tested, being honest about where accuracy degrades.
judge_qna.follow_up: What's the largest sun-angle difference your algorithm still successfully registers?

judge_qna.question: Did you address multi-modal (different sensor) registration, or focus on same-sensor illumination-invariance?
judge_qna.strong_answer: Be direct about your scoping choice, if you focused on illumination-invariance within one sensor type as your primary, achievable demonstration, explain that clearly and what full multi-modal registration would additionally require.
judge_qna.follow_up: What's the biggest additional challenge in registering across genuinely different sensor types (OHRC to IIRS, for example)?
